findings.claim: aicore/tests preserves 26 direct artifacts including 18 substantive Python test/benchmark drivers spanning thalamus, longitudinal/stress behavior, intent queue, immune/accumbens/Titan subsystems, fuzzing, functional checks and architecture-vs-bare comparisons, plus six historical result artifacts.
findings.implication: H1/H2/H3 should adapt representative historical executable fixtures rather than recreating every regression family from prose.

findings.claim: Several tests and benchmarks are also present in Project-Frankenstein history/current tree, so this Drive preservation is corroborative until file-level deltas or deleted variants are proven.
findings.implication: Deduplicate by test semantics/version hash; retain changed/deleted variants as chronology, not duplicate earned work.

findings.claim: The historical atlas already separates subsystem tests, long-horizon stress, fuzz, baseline and comparative evaluation families, supporting a layered harness rather than one aggregate score.
findings.implication: Current release gates should require independent correctness, robustness, longitudinal, causal-lesion and baseline-comparison receipts so failure in one family cannot be hidden by an aggregate average.

progress_accounting.reason: Root atlas frozen; semantic replay/diff and global denominators remain open.
